topics.title: Prove the thesis by shipping.
topics.body: Push existing projects out; the next thing isn't worth building until the current one has reacted-to evidence.

topics.title: "What counts as complete?"
topics.body: The central framing question for the talk in an agentic world.

topics.title: AI augments, doesn't replace.
topics.body: Productivity / value gain belongs to humans. The right response to AI is more people, capitalizing on new capabilities — not fewer.

topics.title: "The point of AI is it's adequate."
topics.body: Ben's LinkedIn premise; Jackson agreed.

topics.title: AI is not magic — it predicts patterns.
topics.body: Tuned to answer questions positively. The party-trick demo (see Anecdotes) collapses the mystique fast.

topics.title: "Just fix it" beats "who broke it."
topics.body: AI dissolves the cost of a fix to the point where blame culture is obsolete. The old "you break it, you own it" mentality made sense when fixing was expensive.

topics.title: AI lets engineers write more fun code, not less.
topics.body: It eats peripheral work — tests, dummy data, ETL glue — and leaves the interesting decisions on the table.

topics.title: Velocity should be reinvested.
topics.body: Faster ship dates aren't the win — better test coverage and scenario planning is.

topics.title: Programmer's value is expertise.
topics.body: Guiding LLMs to better results is the craft. Jackson's 3D-rendering knowledge cracked a MapKit occlusion problem the LLM swore was impossible.

topics.title: Plan mode vs raw prompting.
topics.body: Ben Slack-pasted the whole project description → broken app (missing map, dead buttons). Jackson did contextual prompt → plan mode → trimmed scope review → working app. Demo-able A/B.

topics.title: Cross-model plan review.
topics.body: Use Claude to make a plan, Codex to review pros/cons. Surfaces "conspicuous changes" before code.

topics.title: Throwaway code is fine.
topics.body: Not every line needs a commit; retaining junk confuses future LLM passes.

topics.title: Output styles that summarize discoveries.
topics.body: Skim for red flags without reading every line of generated code.

topics.title: Tag interdependencies for parallel agents.
topics.body: Frame the plan as dev tasks with deps; the planning itself becomes a self-review.

topics.title: Cloud Code > IDE wrappers.
topics.body: Purpose-built tools beat IDE-layered system prompts on top of Opus (e.g. Cursor).

topics.title: Git worktrees for parallel efforts.
topics.body: Multiple agents running side-by-side without stomping on each other.

topics.title: Save chat history.
topics.body: Claude/Codex CLIs persist transcripts. Use them as proof and as presentation material.

topics.title: Time-box the LLM's failures.
topics.body: When 430-of-834 conference fetches failed during tagging: don't dive in fixing — check the successes are reasonable, then ship. "Good enough for now" beats blocking on the long tail.

topics.title: Two-pass tagging (free-form, then taxonomy).
topics.body: Cheap model generates loose tags across all items first; smarter model collapses them into a normalized taxonomy. Avoids over-constraining the first pass.

topics.title: Politeness is cheap.
topics.body: A few extra tokens per prompt; long-term hygiene if it ever matters; doesn't seem to hurt output. Default to polite.

topics.title: AI is like driving on icy roads.
topics.body: The point is to get where you want to go not be in absolute control the entire time.

topics.title: Backend / data structures first.
topics.body: UI is trivial once the API is well-documented and structured.

topics.title: Strong language sometimes improves results.
topics.body: Jackson's anecdote on getting un-stuck after a polite prompt failed.

topics.title: Fewer prompts than expected.
topics.body: Ben's app: ~27 prompts. Jackson's: one-shot from a single specific paragraph.

topics.title: "LLM-speak. Talk to it like it's the average/adequate version of the expert you want it to be."
topics.body: Use the model's own vocabulary back at it. Better outcomes.

topics.title: Phrasing changes the answer.
topics.body: "State-of-the-art" pulls a very different context than "best practice." Word choice is a config knob.

topics.title: Non-directive prompts delegate decisions.
topics.body: "I want…" / "It would be nice if…" gives the model room to choose well, instead of pinning it to a specific implementation that may not match the codebase.

topics.title: AI estimates are human time.
topics.body: It says a change is 1.5 days of work and then finishes it in 90 seconds. Like book hours in mechanics — useful for planning, lousy as a wall-clock predictor.

topics.title: The skill is how to talk to it, not your config.
topics.body: People ask "what's in your Claude.md?" — the wrong question. The reusable skill is interaction style; configs are individual artifacts.

topics.title: AI-simulated frontend/backend team.
topics.body: Ben fed a proposal in and had the model role-play both sides of an engineering debate. Surfaced realistic tradeoffs and practical solutions — a use case nobody pre-AI had access to.

topics.title: Jackson's "told it was impossible" scraper.
topics.body: As VP Eng, no one would build it; he was warned scraping was a fool's errand. Today: tells AI to "figure it out," gets purpose-built code that's better than good enough because it's fitted to four government sites — not a generic reusable system. The throwaway is the win.

topics.title: Apple credit card / Finance Kit API.
topics.body: Jackson's tax-reconciliation pain. Built a tiny app, hit Apple's app-review wall — illustrates platform gatekeeping vs. solo-dev ambition.

topics.title: Anonymous-first auth.
topics.body: You ARE an account on first visit. Google/GitHub buttons aren't sign-up — they're portability upgrades.

topics.title: Stable doc IDs by date-only hash.
topics.body: Lesson learned the hard way: Minnebar dupes from drift across import eras. Talkable failure → fix.

topics.title: Live-build candidates (ranked).
topics.body: Feed of new users/activity (Firestore reactive snapshots), CI/CD pipeline setup, real conference data ETL with AI prompts, Mapbox dot styling.

topics.title: Conference catalog: 652 → 834 → 3,000 target.
topics.body: Sourced from confs.tech, then vendor-flagships, security archives, Wikipedia CS conferences, Linux Foundation, data/ML series, and Minnestar. NA-only target is ~3,000 events.

topics.title: "Drop a demo user when a real user joins."
topics.body: Playful idea — the feed never empties, and the platform telegraphs growth honestly. Wouldn't survive product-grooming, which is part of the charm.

topics.title: Multi-chip search: AND first, OR later.
topics.body: MVP discipline — the default narrows results; the OR (any-of) can come once the AND is right.

topics.title: Don't drag-and-drop, write components.
topics.body: Squarespace / Wizzywig hostility. Time goes to content, not framework selection.

topics.title: Hyper-personalized apps explosion.
topics.body: Number of apps spikes, then declines as AI generates one-off specialized tools on demand.

topics.title: Welcome audience bug reports — even ask for a PR.
topics.body: Reframes "found a bug" from shame to collaboration; matches the "just fix it" theme of the talk.

topics.title: COMING_SOON_ONLY flag.
topics.body: Single const in web/src/main.tsx. Flip to false, push to main, deploy auto-flips audience.

topics.title: Build-number live refresh.
topics.body: bump-version.mjs mutates web/public/version.json; root-level poller in main.tsx reloads on mismatch. Bidirectional (live↔gated).

topics.title: Bidirectional reload trade.
topics.body: Every deploy hard-refreshes everyone with the tab open. Fine for the demo; demote to a "new version available" banner once routine deploys resume.

topics.title: "Cooking show" framing.
topics.body: Some prep is pre-baked; the entire process is in git, so nothing's hidden. Manages expectations and gives you license to skip past plumbing on stage.

topics.title: Be transparent about AI in the PDD itself.
topics.body: Owning the AI-generated spec resonates more than pretending.

topics.title: Live build is the point, not the polished result.
topics.body: Process > artifact. Disingenuous to present a finished product in a from-scratch session.
